CLI for the Health Checks service. Use this CLI to manage endpoint probes and monitors.
For more information, see
[Overview of the Health Checks Service].

http-monitor change-compartment.help:
Moves a monitor into a different compartment. When provided, `If-Match` is checked against ETag values of the resource. 
[Command Reference](changeHttpMonitorCompartment)

params.name: monitor_id
params.help: The OCID of a monitor. [required]

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the compartment into which the resource should be moved. [required]

params.name: if_match
params.help: For optimistic concurrency control. In the PUT or DELETE call for a resource, set the `if-match` parameter to the value of the etag from a previous GET or POST response for that resource.  The resource will be updated or deleted only if the etag you provide matches the resource's current etag value.

http-monitor create.help:
Creates an HTTP monitor. Vantage points will be automatically selected if not specified, and probes will be initiated from each vantage point to each of the targets at the frequency specified by `intervalInSeconds`. 
[Command Reference](createHttpMonitor)

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The OCID of the compartment. [required]

params.name: targets
params.help:
A list of targets (hostnames or IP addresses) of the probe.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.
 [required]

params.name: protocol
params.help: [required]

params.name: display_name
params.help: A user-friendly and mutable name suitable for display in a user interface. [required]

params.name: interval_in_seconds
params.help: The monitor interval in seconds. Valid values: 10, 30, and 60. [required]

params.name: vantage_point_names
params.help:
A list of names of vantage points from which to execute the probe.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: port
params.help: The port on which to probe endpoints. If unspecified, probes will use the default port of their protocol.

params.name: timeout_in_seconds
params.help: The probe timeout in seconds. Valid values: 10, 20, 30, and 60. The probe timeout must be less than or equal to `intervalInSeconds` for monitors.

params.name: path
params.help: The optional URL path to probe, including query parameters.

params.name: headers
params.help:
A dictionary of HTTP request headers.

*Note:* Monitors and probes do not support the use of the `Authorization` HTTP header.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: is_enabled
params.help: Enables or disables the monitor. Set to 'true' to launch monitoring.

params.help:
